desc:
You are given a binary string s. You may first rotate it any number of times for free; one rotation moves the first character to the end (so "1100" becomes "1001", then "0011", and so on). After choosing how many rotations to apply, you may flip single characters ('0' to '1' or the other way) at a cost of one flip each.

Return the minimum number of flips needed so that the resulting string is alternating, meaning no two adjacent characters are equal. The result is judged as a plain string; the string is not considered circular.

For example, s = "111000" gives 2, s = "110" gives 0 (rotate once to get 101), and s = "0000" gives 2.
constraints: s contains only the characters '0' and '1'
hints: Without rotations the answer is min(m, n - m), where m is the number of mismatches with 0101.... With rotations you have n different strings to evaluate this for.
Trying every rotation and recounting costs O(n2). To go faster, notice that every rotation of s appears as a window of length n inside s + s.

Compare s + s with the fixed pattern 0101... and build prefix sums of the mismatches. The mismatches of the window starting at i against 0101... (or, for odd i, its complement) are then a difference of two prefix sums; take min(m, n - m) for each window.
editorial: Every rotation of s is the window (s + s)[i : i + n] for some i between 0 and n - 1. For one window, the cost is min(m, n - m) where m is the number of positions at which the window disagrees with the pattern 0101... started at the window's own first character.

Instead of rebuilding the pattern for every window, compare s + s once with the global pattern A[j] = j % 2 and let mis[j] be 1 when they differ. The window starting at i has M mismatches with the global pattern, which is a prefix-sum difference. If i is even, the window's own pattern is the global one, so m = M; if i is odd the window's own pattern is the complement of the global one and m = n - M. Either way min(m, n - m) = min(M, n - M), so the parity of i does not matter.
That gives an O(n) time, O(n) space algorithm (a sliding window would use O(1) extra space).
solution:
def minFlipsRotation(s):
    n = len(s)
    t = s + s
    pre = [0] * (2 * n + 1)
    for j, c in enumerate(t):
        pre[j + 1] = pre[j] + (1 if int(c) != j % 2 else 0)
    best = n
    for i in range(n):
        m = pre[i + n] - pre[i]
        best = min(best, m, n - m)
    return best
